privileged_keys.name: SANDY_SSH
privileged_keys.description: SSH auth mode: 'token' uses gh CLI (HTTPS); 'agent' forwards the host SSH agent.

privileged_keys.name: SANDY_SSH_KEYS
privileged_keys.description: Comma-separated FILENAMES under ~/.ssh that may be staged into the container, in ANY SANDY_SSH mode. Default empty = no private key material is staged at all. Only these files, plus config, known_hosts and *.pub, reach the container; everything else in ~/.ssh stays on the host. A name matching no file is warned about rather than silently ignored. Forced empty by SANDY_SUSPICIOUS=1.

privileged_keys.name: SANDY_SKIP_PERMISSIONS
privileged_keys.description: Skip Claude Code's in-session permission prompts (default: true).

privileged_keys.name: SANDY_ALLOW_NO_ISOLATION
privileged_keys.description: Allow launch when iptables rules cannot be applied (Linux only).

privileged_keys.name: SANDY_ALLOW_LAN_HOSTS
privileged_keys.description: Comma-separated IPs/CIDRs to allow through LAN isolation. World-open entries rejected.

privileged_keys.name: SANDY_LOCAL_LLM_HOST
privileged_keys.description: Single host:port (e.g. '127.0.0.1:11434') to allow through LAN isolation, typically for a local LLM. With the egress proxy on (default) the proxy's forward listener relays host.docker.internal:<port> to the host; with the proxy off (=0, Linux) it inserts one iptables ACCEPT and maps host.docker.internal.

privileged_keys.name: SANDY_ALLOW_HOSTS
privileged_keys.description: Comma-separated extra egress-proxy allowlist entries (exact host, '*.suffix' wildcard, or 'host:port' for CONNECT/SSH). Appended to the built-in default allowlist. In strict mode (SANDY_EGRESS_PROXY=2) these are the only hosts reachable beyond defaults; in permissive mode (=1) they are LAN-exceptions reachable despite the private-IP block. Privileged tier so workspace config requires approval.

privileged_keys.name: SANDY_EXTRA_ENV
privileged_keys.description: Comma-separated env-var names to forward into the container (e.g. 'HA_TOKEN,FOO_API_KEY'). The name lists COMPOSE (2.4.0): the effective list is the union of the host lists, any approved workspace list, and an env-set list (env ADDS, it does not replace), deduplicated in that order. Values resolve env > workspace .sandy/.secrets > workspace .sandy/config > ~/.sandy/.secrets > ~/.sandy/config. The privileged tier gates the NAME list (workspace config setting SANDY_EXTRA_ENV itself requires approval); once approved, values may come from any source.

privileged_keys.name: SANDY_AGENT_ARGS
privileged_keys.description: Extra command-line arguments appended to the agent command (claude/codex/gemini/opencode) on EVERY launch — bare sandy, headless -p, the --start daemon, and sandy-ui alike. Whitespace-split into argv (no embedded-space/quoting support in v1) and forwarded through the same per-agent translation as command-line pass-through args, ordered AFTER sandy's own flags and BEFORE any command-line args. Privileged tier: free from host ~/.sandy/config, but from a workspace .sandy/config it triggers the per-workspace approval prompt (headless/non-TTY drops it). Never eval'd. Typical use: a fixed --mcp-config <path> or project feature flags. Applies to every selected agent (each pane in a multi-agent combo) unless overridden per agent by an operator file $SANDBOX_DIR/agent-args.<agent> (sandbox top level, agent-unwritable, privileged by location — no prompt); when both are present the sandbox file wins for that agent, values are never merged, and sandy prints a one-line notice.

privileged_keys.name: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY
privileged_keys.description: Anthropic API key for Claude Code. Not required when using Claude Max OAuth.

privileged_keys.name: CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN
privileged_keys.description: Claude Code OAuth token (alternative to ANTHROPIC_API_KEY).

privileged_keys.name: GEMINI_API_KEY

privileged_keys.name: OPENAI_API_KEY

privileged_keys.name: XAI_API_KEY
privileged_keys.description: xAI API key for Grok Build (docs.x.ai). Enables fully-headless auth (resolution: model.api_key > env_key > session token > XAI_API_KEY); alternative is an interactive 'grok login' OAuth session inside the container.

privileged_keys.name: GOOGLE_API_KEY
privileged_keys.description: Google API key for Vertex AI / ADC.

privileged_keys.name: CLAUDE_CODE_EXPERIMENTAL_AGENT_TEAMS
privileged_keys.description: Enable Claude Code experimental agent-teams feature.

privileged_keys.name: SANDY_SCREENSHOT_DIR
privileged_keys.description: Host directory containing screenshots; mounted read-only at /home/sandy/screenshots and exposed as $SANDY_SCREENSHOTS_PATH inside the container. Enables /ss skill across agents.

privileged_keys.name: SANDY_GEMINI_EXTENSIONS
privileged_keys.description: Comma-separated Gemini extensions to enable.

privileged_keys.name: TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN
privileged_keys.description: Telegram bot token for the channel relay.

privileged_keys.name: TELEGRAM_ALLOWED_SENDERS
privileged_keys.description: Comma-separated Telegram user IDs allowed to send messages.

privileged_keys.name: DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN
privileged_keys.description: Discord bot token for the channel relay.

privileged_keys.name: DISCORD_ALLOWED_SENDERS
privileged_keys.description: Comma-separated Discord user IDs allowed to send messages.

privileged_keys.name: SANDY_HANDOFF_RELAY
privileged_keys.description: REMOVED AS A CONFIGURATION KEY in 2.2.0 (#354) -- setting it from the environment or any config file is a HARD ERROR naming the replacement (declare the executable as an 'entry' in a feature manifest). The INTERNAL CHANNEL it later served -- carrying the relay-designated entry's path from host to container-side supervisor -- was itself removed in 2.6.0 (#382, decisions 4-5): the host now passes every adopted entry to the container only via SANDY_FEATURE_ENTRIES (internal, no metadata row; see 'feature_entries' below), and no entry is designated any more -- every entry is supervised and reported identically. What an entry gets: a container-level process (a sibling of the tmux server, not a pane, not a child of any agent session), started once per container by user-setup.sh before the tmux session exists (never in headless -p runs, never under --remote, never under --provision), held to one instance by flock, restarted on death with exponential backoff (1s doubling to 60s, reset after a 60s+ run), never given up on. Every entry's state (.state, supervisor.log) lives at its own $SANDBOX_DIR/feature-state/<feature>, mounted rw at /opt/sandy/feature-state/<feature> and exported to that entry's own process as SANDY_FEATURE_STATE -- an entry reads its own directory from that variable rather than constructing the path, uniform across every entry. Env contract: SANDY_FEATURE_STATE, SANDY_AGENT, SANDY_WORKSPACE. An entry that cannot start FAILS THE LAUNCH, never warn-and-proceed: missing or not executable, its state dir not mounted, or no flock (user-setup.sh exits 1, the container dies, --start reports crash-looping/exit 7) -- one shared 5s startup window covers every entry at once. DOCUMENTED EXCEPTION: a stale image predating per-feature entries (a deferred build per #218, or any other image built before the sandy.feature_entries=1 Dockerfile label existed) knows only the removed SANDY_HANDOFF_RELAY channel and so starts NONE of the entries -- sandy warns at launch, naming every one, and --print-state reports them all as state absent. There is no runtime toggle to stop them: SANDY_RELAY is a HARD ERROR as of 2.6.0 (see its own row below) with no per-feature replacement, so every adopted entry always runs. Reported in /etc/sandy-session.json as feature_entries.<feature>.{path} -- schema_version 4 (2.6.0, #382, decisions 1-2): relay{} itself, and its two companions relay_alias and disabled_by, are gone from both the marker and --print-state -- and live in --print-state as feature_entries.<feature>.state (every entry, identically). In daemon mode an entry (and anything else planted at the uid) outlives sessions until the container is recreated -- run sandy --update-sessions --yes on a 24h cron.

privileged_keys.name: ANTHROPIC_PROFILE
privileged_keys.description: Privileged. Name of the Anthropic Console profile to use when SANDY_CLAUDE_AUTH=profile (overrides the host active_config); forwarded into the container so Claude Code selects it explicitly (its /status shows the Profile row as profile-explicit). Privileged on purpose: it chooses WHICH profile's token enters the box, and a profile logged in with --scope org:admin carries organization-wide access, so a committed .sandy/config must not be able to select it. Ignored with a notice unless SANDY_CLAUDE_AUTH=profile.

passive_keys.name: SANDY_AGENT
passive_keys.description: Agent(s) to launch. Comma-separated (e.g. 'claude,codex'). 'all' = 'claude,gemini,codex,opencode'.

passive_keys.name: SANDY_MODEL
passive_keys.description: Model ID for the Claude agent.

passive_keys.name: SANDY_TEAMMATE_MODE
passive_keys.description: Value passed to 'claude --teammate-mode' (claude only). Empty by default, so sandy does NOT pass the flag and Claude Code uses its own default. Set e.g. 'tmux' to opt in; 'off' or 'none' are also treated as omit. Passive-safe (teammate mode does not affect isolation). Sandy does not seed teammateMode into settings.json either — this flag governs the session, and a host settings.json value is left untouched.

passive_keys.name: SANDY_EFFORT
passive_keys.description: Reasoning effort for claude, (2.4.0) codex, and (2.7.0) grok and gemini. Claude: 'claude --effort <level>'; levels are model-dependent and an unsupported level falls back to the highest supported at or below it. Codex: '-c model_reasoning_effort=<level>', each sandy level mapped to its exact codex namesake (max -> max, codex's top non-delegating level; never ultra, which adds multi-agent delegation); whether a codex model offers the level is codex's catalog's business. Grok: '--reasoning-effort <level>' (alias --effort; a top-level option, so TUI and headless alike), low/medium/high/xhigh passed as-is and max CLAMPED to xhigh with a launch notice, because grok rejects max outright. Gemini (no flag): a sandy-generated, read-only system settings file named by GEMINI_CLI_SYSTEM_SETTINGS_PATH, holding only modelConfigs.customOverrides -- Gemini 3 thinkingLevel LOW for low and HIGH otherwise, Gemini 2.5 thinkingBudget 1024/8192/24576 for low/medium/high-and-above; it outranks user and workspace gemini settings and shadows a user's own modelConfigs.customOverrides while set. Empty leaves each agent's own default. Ignored, with a notice, for a launch with none of claude, codex, grok or gemini (opencode has no effort surface sandy drives). Passive-safe (effort does not affect isolation). Recorded in sandy-session.json as the sandy-level value.

passive_keys.name: SANDY_CPUS
passive_keys.description: CPU limit for container (default: auto-detected).

passive_keys.name: SANDY_MEM
passive_keys.description: Memory limit for container (e.g. '8g'; default: auto-detected).

passive_keys.name: SANDY_GPU
passive_keys.description: GPU passthrough: 'all', or device IDs like '0' / '0,1'.

passive_keys.name: SANDY_SKILL_PACKS
passive_keys.description: Comma-separated skill pack names (e.g. 'gstack').

passive_keys.name: SANDY_CHANNELS
passive_keys.description: Comma-separated channel names (e.g. 'telegram,discord').

passive_keys.name: SANDY_CHANNEL_TARGET_PANE
passive_keys.description: Which agent's pane receives Telegram host-relay messages in multi-agent mode: a 0-based position in SANDY_AGENT (0 = first agent, up to 3), resolved to the pane tagged with that agent -- not a raw tmux pane index, which differs from spawn order in the 2x2 grid.

passive_keys.name: SANDY_VERBOSE
passive_keys.description: Verbosity (0=quiet, 1=verbose, 2=debug, 3=full trace).

passive_keys.name: SANDY_VENV_OVERLAY
passive_keys.description: Bind-mount a sandbox-owned .venv over the workspace's .venv inside the container.

passive_keys.name: SANDY_EGRESS
passive_keys.description: Egress posture, ONE key as of 2.0.0. off = proxy off (legacy: Linux iptables only, NO network isolation on macOS). permissive (default) = proxy on, blocking private/LAN/link-local/CGNAT/cloud-metadata destinations while allowing the internet. strict = proxy on with an allowlist only (model providers, GitHub, npm, PyPI, crates, Go, Debian) plus SANDY_ALLOW_HOSTS. Replaces a three-way choice encoded as TWO MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE BOOLEANS (SANDY_EGRESS_NO_ISOLATION, SANDY_EGRESS_STRICT) plus a deprecated tri-state whose 0/1/2 were opaque (SANDY_EGRESS_PROXY) -- all three still work, are listed in README's Deprecated section, and are IGNORED WITH A NOTICE when this key is set (never merged; the winner is named). Value-aware tier: only strict is passive-safe. off and permissive are approval-gated from a workspace .sandy/config, exactly as SANDY_EGRESS_NO_ISOLATION=1 and SANDY_EGRESS_STRICT=0 are -- a workspace value outranks the host config for the same key, so an ungated permissive would silently downgrade a host that chose strict (#371, fixed in 2.4.0; 2.0.0-2.3.x gated only off). Like STRICT=0 it prompts even where the host is already permissive. SANDY_SUSPICIOUS=1 still defaults the posture to strict; an explicit choice wins and a weaker one is named loudly.

passive_keys.name: SANDY_EGRESS_PROXY
passive_keys.description: DEPRECATED — use SANDY_EGRESS=off,permissive,strict. Kept as a back-compat alias: 0->NO_ISOLATION=1 (off), 1->permissive (default), 2->STRICT=1 (strict). From a workspace .sandy/config, =0 (off) and =1 (permissive: a downgrade of a host-set =2) are approval-gated, matching SANDY_EGRESS; only =2 is free (#371).

passive_keys.name: SANDY_EGRESS_NO_ISOLATION
passive_keys.description: Turn the egress proxy OFF — legacy path (Linux iptables-only; NO network isolation on macOS). WEAKENS isolation, so from a workspace .sandy/config it is quarantined to the per-workspace approval prompt (a committed config cannot silently disable isolation). Mutually exclusive with SANDY_EGRESS_STRICT. Default 0 (proxy on).

passive_keys.name: SANDY_EGRESS_STRICT
passive_keys.description: Run the egress proxy in strict mode (allow only the built-in default allowlist + SANDY_ALLOW_HOSTS; deny all other internet). STRENGTHENS isolation, so =1 is passive-safe from any source; =0 (downgrading a host-configured strict) is approval-gated from a workspace source. Mutually exclusive with SANDY_EGRESS_NO_ISOLATION. Default 0 (permissive).

passive_keys.name: SANDY_EGRESS_LOG
passive_keys.description: Log which hosts the agent's egress actually reached (HF-incident Issue 4). The proxy logs each DISTINCT allowed host:port once (deduped) to proxy.log; at session end sandy prints an egress summary (distinct hosts reached + denial count). 0=off (deny-only, the pre-1.4 behavior); 1=per-connection allow lines + session-end summary; summary=session-end summary only (the proxy still records allows to build it). Passive-safe: it only ADDS visibility. Hostnames only — TLS is never terminated, no payload; the log stays in $SANDBOX_DIR.

passive_keys.name: SANDY_ALLOW_WORKFLOW_EDIT
passive_keys.description: Remove .github/workflows from the read-only protection list.

passive_keys.name: CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS
passive_keys.description: Max output tokens per Claude response.

passive_keys.name: CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL
passive_keys.description: Model ID for Claude Code SUBAGENTS -- the parallel researchers a skill fans out. Subagents do NOT inherit the orchestrator model, so unset they run on their own default tier: a session pinned to a gated model (e.g. claude-mythos-5-1) silently does its fan-out work on a different one, with nothing in the transcript saying so. Passive-safe: a model ID is not a capability and can only select a model the session credential is already entitled to.

passive_keys.name: GEMINI_MODEL
passive_keys.description: Gemini model override.

passive_keys.name: SANDY_GEMINI_AUTH
passive_keys.description: Gemini credential probe strategy.

passive_keys.name: GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT
passive_keys.description: Google Cloud project for Vertex AI.

passive_keys.name: GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION
passive_keys.description: Google Cloud location for Vertex AI.

passive_keys.name: GOOGLE_GENAI_USE_VERTEXAI
passive_keys.description: Use Vertex AI backend for Gemini.

passive_keys.name: CODEX_MODEL
passive_keys.description: Codex model override.

passive_keys.name: SANDY_CODEX_AUTH
passive_keys.description: Codex credential probe strategy.

passive_keys.name: OPENCODE_MODEL
passive_keys.description: OpenCode model override (provider/model format, e.g. 'anthropic/claude-sonnet-4').

passive_keys.name: SANDY_OPENCODE_AUTH
passive_keys.description: OpenCode credential probe strategy.

passive_keys.name: GROK_MODEL
passive_keys.description: Grok Build model override (passed as -m; default grok-4.5).

passive_keys.name: SANDY_GROK_AUTH
passive_keys.description: Grok Build credential probe strategy.

passive_keys.name: SANDY_CLAUDE_AUTH
passive_keys.description: Claude Code credential selection. auto (default): a long-lived CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN wins, else the host OAuth credentials file is mounted and ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is SUPPRESSED (Claude Code resolves an env key ahead of the account credentials, so forwarding both either bills per-use or parks the session on the custom-API-key startup modal). api_key: forward ANTHROPIC_API_KEY and do NOT mount OAuth credentials -- a revocable project key instead of the account refresh token, and the only way to choose per-use billing on a host that has OAuth. oauth: mount OAuth and never forward the API key or a long-lived CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN (2.8.0, #437): the account login is the only Claude credential in the box, which is also what claude.ai connectors need; with no account login on the host it falls back to the token, with a warning. profile (1.11.0): use an Anthropic Console profile written by `ant auth login` (the Claude Platform CLI) -- the ONLY way to reach a workspace-bound entitlement such as Claude Mythos. Sandy copies just the selected profile (ANTHROPIC_PROFILE, else the host active_config, else default) from $ANTHROPIC_CONFIG_DIR (default ~/.config/anthropic) into an ephemeral rw mount at ~/.config/anthropic and withholds the OAuth credentials file, CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN and ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, because Claude Code ranks a user_oauth profile BELOW a /login credential and below every env credential -- measured on 2.1.263. Never probed by auto. Value-aware tier: api_key, profile and auto are passive-safe (each REDUCES what is in the container), while oauth from a workspace is approval-gated because it forces the account-scoped credential in even when a revocable key is available.

passive_keys.name: SANDY_TOOL_AUDIT
passive_keys.description: Seed a Claude Code PreToolUse audit hook (HF-incident Issue 6) that appends {ts,tool,args} JSONL to ~/.claude/tool-audit.jsonl for per-session tool-use telemetry — instrumenting the agent harness itself, not just the box. Only-if-absent: a user's own PreToolUse hook is never clobbered. Passive-safe (only ADDS visibility). Claude-only (no equivalent seam for codex/gemini/opencode). Not tamper-proof against a determined agent (runs in-box) — telemetry for the primary wrong-but-not-evil adversary. Default 0 (off).

passive_keys.name: SANDY_CLAUDE_CONNECTORS
passive_keys.description: Expose the claude.ai ACCOUNT connectors (Gmail, Google Drive, ...) inside the sandbox (#129). Default 0 = SUPPRESSED. The OAuth token sandy mounts is account-scoped, so without this every connector the user ever enabled on claude.ai was reachable from EVERY sandbox -- including untrusted-repo sessions, with no extra prompt -- which is ambient authority crossing the per-project boundary sandy exists to draw. Implemented by seeding Claude Code's disableClaudeAiConnectors as a MANAGED settings.json key (always overwritten, both directions): Claude resolves it true-in-ANY-settings-scope-wins, so writing false is not enough to expose them -- an inherited true from the host settings.json would win. VALUE-AWARE TIER: 0 is passive-safe wherever it is set, but =1 WEAKENS the sandbox, so a workspace .sandy/config setting it triggers the per-workspace approval prompt like SANDY_EGRESS_NO_ISOLATION=1. Claude-only (the account-connector rider is a Claude Code phenomenon); gates AUTO-FETCHED connectors only -- a server passed explicitly via --mcp-config still follows the normal MCP trust flow.

passive_keys.name: SANDY_SUSPICIOUS
passive_keys.description: Hardened-credential posture for a workspace you actively distrust (#130) -- the pre-broker slice of #121. When 1: (a) the mounted Claude .credentials.json is REWRITTEN to drop claudeAiOauth.refreshToken, so an exfiltrated copy is worth only the remaining access-token lifetime (hours) instead of permanent renewable account access; the strip is verified after the rewrite and FAILS CLOSED -- if it cannot be performed or verified, no credentials file is mounted at all; (b) if ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is set and no long-lived CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN is, the API key is used and OAuth credentials are not mounted (clean, instantly-revocable compartmentalization); (c) claude.ai account connectors are forced off, overriding an approved SANDY_CLAUDE_CONNECTORS=1; (d) egress DEFAULTS to strict -- an explicit egress setting still wins but is named loudly. Since 1.12.0 this also covers SANDY_CLAUDE_AUTH=profile (#252): the ephemeral copy of the Console profile has its refresh_token stripped (the host profile is never touched) and cred_mode becomes profile-access-only; a strip that cannot be performed or verified mounts NO profile at all. The resolved posture is recorded as cred_mode in /etc/sandy-session.json so a run protection level is provable after the fact. Passive-safe to turn ON from a committed .sandy/config (a repo may make itself tighter); =0 from a workspace is approval-gated (never looser). HONEST LIMITS: in-session token refresh stops working once the access token expires (rerun sandy or /login -- acceptable for a deliberately short suspicious session); a long-lived CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN is NOT shrunk by this (recorded honestly as cred_mode oauth-token, with a warning); Claude-only for the credential specifics; real prevention (token never in-container) is #121.

passive_keys.name: SANDY_CROSS_SESSION_INBOUND
passive_keys.description: Claude-only. Pins Claude Code crossSessionInbound (accept = deliver messages from other sessions on this container without a prompt; hold = queue for approval; refuse = drop with a sender-visible status) by writing the SAME resolved value into TWO places every launch, merge-preserving and idempotent: the sandbox's own claude/settings.json (mounted RW as the container's ~/.claude/settings.json, i.e. Claude Code userSettings) and the WORKSPACE project file .claude/settings.local.json (mounted :ro). This split is measured, not assumed, against Claude Code 2.1.251: accept only takes effect when present in userSettings (workspace-file accept alone is a no-op there); hold/refuse are honored from either, and the workspace file's copy is tighten-only so it cannot be loosened by a stale accept and still wins over userSettings when a repo hand-edits it stricter. Never writes ~/.claude/settings.json on the HOST. Default is CONDITIONAL, which is why the schema default is empty, and as of 2.4.0 (#380) it is keyed on a DECLARED NEED rather than on any entry: accept iff a SELECTED feature manifest declares `"receives": ["cross_session"]` AND this is not a headless (-p), --remote or --provision run (none of those leave a session for anything to deliver into), else refuse. An entry alone, with no feature declaring the need, resolves refuse. (Pre-2.6.0 sandy also accepted on the strength of a feature entry alone -- announced for removal in README's Deprecated table in 2.5.0 (#382) and removed in 2.6.0; see CLAUDE.md "Cross-session inbound".) A declared need is independent of whether any entry process runs at all -- `receives` is its own, separate, privileged statement of what a feature needs to receive, decoupled from whether that feature ships an `entry`. Value-aware tier: hold and refuse are passive-safe wherever set; accept set via a workspace .sandy/config is approval-gated (it lets any process at the workspace uid inside the container inject a turn) -- unchanged, whichever default path resolved it. Residual: the userSettings target is RW in-container (required for /plugin install), so unlike the :ro workspace copy it is agent-mutable mid-session; sandy resets it on the next launch, not mid-session. Recorded in /etc/sandy-session.json as cross_session_inbound, with cross_session_inbound_source (one of explicit, feature:<name> or default) naming WHY. See docs/security/CROSS_SESSION_INBOUND.md.

passive_keys.name: SANDY_RELAY
passive_keys.description: REMOVED in 2.6.0 (#382) after its 2.5.0 announcement: setting it from ANY source (environment, host config or a workspace .sandy/config), to any value, is a HARD ERROR naming the replacement -- add the sandbox to a feature manifest's "sandboxes": {"exclude": [...]}. There is deliberately no per-feature off switch and no replacement key. The key stays in the passive tier only so the loader recognizes it and fails rather than silently ignoring it as unknown.

passive_keys.name: SANDY_OFFLINE
passive_keys.description: Offline mode (#219): skip the lookups a launch makes only to learn whether something NEWER exists -- the per-agent version checks (a hit forces a --no-cache agent rebuild), skill-pack version resolution from GitHub (falls back to the local cache, then the built-in pin), and sandy's own release nag. Builds that are REQUIRED still run: a missing image or a changed Dockerfile builds through the build-reachability gate and fails there as it always has. For a known-bad network (in-flight wifi, captive portal) or an air-gapped host, where the checks cost latency and a detected update would force a rebuild that cannot succeed. The one-shot CLI form is --no-update-check, which wins over this key. Passive-safe: it defers the auto-patch pickup the wrapped-agent CVE posture relies on, but only until the next launch without it -- equivalent to not relaunching -- and it is never silent: one line at launch, one at session end, and 'offline': true in /etc/sandy-session.json. Default 0.

env_only_keys.name: SANDY_AUTO_APPROVE_PRIVILEGED
env_only_keys.description: Bypass TWO of the three launch approval gates: the passive-privileged config-key prompt AND the per-project .sandy/Dockerfile build prompt (an unreviewed project image then builds, running its RUN commands on the host docker daemon with unfiltered network). It does NOT bypass the dangerous-symlink gate, deliberately: that gate is built so no approval of a new escaping symlink can happen without a deliberate human act (a new escape is a hard error, never a re-prompt), and a blanket bypass would silently mount every future escape read-write. Env-only, so a committed config cannot set it. Intended for CI / test harnesses only.

env_only_keys.name: SANDY_CHANNEL
env_only_keys.description: Which build `sandy --upgrade` installs (install.sh reads the same variable). release (default): the latest GitHub release, the version the update notice names; a dev or rc build newer than that release is left alone unless release is set explicitly. dev: the head of main, pinned to its commit and recording it, so --version tells dev builds apart and the next dev upgrade compares commits. Env-only: it is read before any config file is loaded. A failed release lookup is an error, never a silent fallback to main.

env_only_keys.name: SANDY_DEBUG_CLEANUP
env_only_keys.description: Print session-stub cleanup diagnostics on exit.

env_only_keys.name: SANDY_HOST_ID
env_only_keys.description: Operator override for the host_id reported by --print-state (#179), advisory identity for multi-host fleet aggregation (sandbox names hash only the workspace path, so the same path on two hosts collides). ENV-ONLY -- a committed .sandy/config can never set it, which would otherwise forge the identity of whatever machine the repo is cloned onto. Default is uname -n (host_id_source: hostname); a valid override reports host_id_source: env. Invalid or empty values are silently ignored and fall back to uname -n -- no warning, ever, since --print-state guarantees 0 bytes of stderr.

cli_flags.name: --rebuild
cli_flags.description: Force rebuild of sandy images.

cli_flags.name: --build-only
cli_flags.description: Build images and exit (for CI).

cli_flags.name: --no-update-check
cli_flags.description: One-shot SANDY_OFFLINE=1 (#219): skip the agent, skill-pack and sandy release lookups for this launch. Builds that are REQUIRED (missing image, changed inputs) still run. Honored by the bare launch path, -p, --build-only and --start; wins over SANDY_OFFLINE=0 in any config file.

cli_flags.name: --new
cli_flags.description: Start a fresh session (default: resume last). Applies to claude and (#427) codex, which resumes with codex resume --last when this sandbox holds an interactive codex session for the workspace.

cli_flags.name: --resume
cli_flags.description: Open session picker. For codex (#427) this is codex resume, its own picker.

cli_flags.name: --remote
cli_flags.description: Run as a remote-controlled Claude session.

cli_flags.name: --upgrade
cli_flags.description: Self-update sandy to the latest GitHub release, the version the update notice names. Does not downgrade a dev or rc build that is newer than that release unless SANDY_CHANNEL=release is set. SANDY_CHANNEL=dev installs the head of main instead, pinned to its commit and recording it. A failed lookup exits 1 and never falls back to main.

cli_flags.name: --agent
cli_flags.description: Agent(s) for this run (overrides SANDY_AGENT).

cli_flags.name: --help
cli_flags.description: Show help.

cli_flags.name: --version
cli_flags.description: Show version.

cli_flags.name: --print-schema
cli_flags.description: Emit the static introspection schema as JSON.

cli_flags.name: --print-state
cli_flags.description: Emit runtime state (sandboxes, approvals, containers) as JSON.

cli_flags.name: --validate-config
cli_flags.description: Validate a config file against the schema; emit JSON.

cli_flags.name: --print-version
cli_flags.description: Emit machine-readable version JSON (schema_version, version, commit, full_version). full_version is the stable cache key for --print-schema consumers — unlike version, it changes on every commit.

cli_flags.name: --approvals
cli_flags.description: Report, as one JSON document, what each launch approval gate (privileged workspace config keys, symlinks escaping the workspace, the .sandy/Dockerfile build) would decide for a workspace: approved, pending, changed, refused or not_applicable. Judged by the launch path itself (the combined workspace config and .secrets, minus keys the environment sets); key names only, never values. Read-only: grants nothing, writes nothing, needs no Docker. Exit 0 when nothing is unresolved, 2 when a gate would be withheld or refused, 1 when no report could be produced. Sub-options: --workspace PATH.

cli_flags.name: --accounts
cli_flags.description: Report which Anthropic account each sandbox Claude Code is signed in to: email, organization and plan (organization type, seat tier and rate-limit tier), plus the credential mode the last launch used and whether a session holds the sandbox now. Read from the oauthAccount block Claude Code records in each sandbox .claude.json, so it is what Claude Code last recorded there, not a live query. Filesystem only: no Docker. A table by default; --json emits one JSON document. Prints personal data (email). Sub-options: --json, --workspace PATH.

cli_flags.name: --start
cli_flags.description: Start a detached daemon session for the workspace and return once attachable.

cli_flags.name: --attach
cli_flags.description: Attach an interactive client to a running daemon session.

cli_flags.name: --stop
cli_flags.description: Stop a running daemon session (full teardown).

cli_flags.name: --exec
cli_flags.description: Open a shell (or run one command) inside this workspace running container, as the HOST uid. Exists because the hand-rolled form is wrong: docker resolves -u <name> against the image, where the user is uid 1001, while sandy bind-mounts a passwd carrying the host uid -- so docker exec -u sandy yields uid 1001, prints I have no name!, and writes to the workspace mount as the wrong owner. Finds a labelled daemon container first, then a foreground one by exact name. Sub-options: --workspace PATH, --dry-run (print the docker exec command, run nothing), -- CMD... (default /bin/bash).

cli_flags.name: --login
cli_flags.description: Log an agent in so its credential persists in this workspace sandbox (#428). Supported: codex, via codex login --device-auth (the plain form waits on a localhost callback a host browser cannot reach). Runs inside the workspace running container when one mounts the sandbox codex home rw, else as a one-shot launch whose only pane runs the login with OPENAI_API_KEY withheld. Other agents get an error naming their own route. Needs a terminal. Sub-options: --workspace PATH, --dry-run (print the route, run nothing).

cli_flags.name: --prune-orphans
cli_flags.description: Reap orphaned sandy_* networks (dead-owner, no attached container) and exit.

cli_flags.name: --stop-all
cli_flags.description: Fleet emergency stop: enumerate every daemon session on the host and stop each via the hardened per-session teardown. Sub-options: --dry-run, --yes.

cli_flags.name: --gc
cli_flags.description: One-shot global reclaim: dead-owner containers, orphaned sandy_* networks, orphaned per-project/skill images, and dangling sandy images. Sub-options: --dry-run, --yes.

cli_flags.name: --update-sessions
cli_flags.description: Fleet image refresh + rolling restart across every daemon session on the host; scope to one session with --workspace PATH. Sub-options: --dry-run, --yes, --idle-for <minutes>, --rebuild, --workspace.

cli_flags.name: --reset-sandbox
cli_flags.description: Rebuild one project sandbox from a known-good skeleton: destroy its persistent package/agent state (preserving WORKSPACE.json lineage), refusing while a live session holds it. Sub-options: --workspace PATH, --all (every known sandbox, composing the per-workspace form verbatim; the one command for a major upgrade), --keep-history / --purge-history (keep or wipe claude/projects/ — Claude session transcripts and auto-memory — and NOTHING else: the plan names every other non-regenerable entry the reset destroys even with --keep-history; asked interactively, REQUIRED non-interactively, deliberately NOT answered by --yes, and never asked at all under --dry-run, which reports the question as unanswered), --keep-approvals, --dry-run, --yes.

cli_flags.name: --remove-sandbox
cli_flags.description: Permanently delete a sandbox directory (preserves NOTHING, unlike --reset-sandbox). Three mutually exclusive selectors: default/--workspace PATH (workspace must still exist), --sandbox NAME (a sandbox whose workspace is gone), --orphans (every sandbox whose recorded workspace_path no longer exists). Filesystem-only. Sub-options: --workspace PATH, --sandbox NAME, --orphans, --dry-run, --yes.

cli_flags.name: --rsync
cli_flags.description: COPY this workspace sandbox to another host over ssh + rsync (the source is never modified), renamed for the destination workspace path, since the sandbox name hashes it. Rewrites the path-keyed state a hand copy gets wrong: session history and auto-memory in claude/projects/ (renamed when the container path changes), the sibling .claude.json projects key, and WORKSPACE.json (so --remove-sandbox --orphans there cannot mistake it for an orphan). The destination workspace defaults to the same path relative to $HOME and must already exist there. Credential-bearing files are copied and named in the plan; on a CPU architecture mismatch cargo/go/npm-global/pip/uv/venv are skipped. Refuses while a live session holds the workspace and never overwrites a sandbox already on the destination. Takes the destination host as its argument. Sub-options: --workspace PATH, --dest-workspace PATH, --dest-sandy-home PATH, --dry-run, --yes.

cli_flags.name: --rsync-from
cli_flags.description: The reverse of --rsync (#409): PULL a sandbox from another host into this one, over outbound ssh + rsync from here only (the source is never modified). The copy is named for THIS host workspace path and gets the same rewrites as --rsync: session history and auto-memory in claude/projects/ (renamed when the container path changes), the sibling .claude.json projects key, and WORKSPACE.json. The source workspace defaults to the same path relative to $HOME on the remote; the local workspace (--workspace, else the current directory) must already exist. Credential-bearing files are copied and named in the plan; on a CPU architecture mismatch cargo/go/npm-global/pip/uv/venv are skipped. It lands in a hidden staging directory and is renamed into place only once every step succeeds, so a failed pull installs nothing. Refuses while a live session holds the source on the remote and never overwrites a sandbox already here. Takes the source host as its argument. Sub-options: --workspace PATH, --src-workspace PATH, --src-sandy-home PATH, --dry-run, --yes.

cli_flags.name: --doctor
cli_flags.description: Standalone host + runtime readiness check. HOST runs the same checks as doctor.sh (git, curl, docker, PATH, credentials); RUNTIME reuses the sandy predicates verbatim (running-container image staleness, orphaned Docker resources, workspace-lock sanity, orphaned sandboxes -- all read-only findings, never required failures). Exit 0 iff every required HOST check passes; warnings from either section never fail it. Sub-options: --fix, --yes.

cli_flags.name: --provision
cli_flags.description: Non-interactively materialize one workspace sandbox by running the REAL launch path once (start a detached daemon session, confirm it is up, then stop it) — never a flag that fabricates sandbox state directly. Safe no-op (exit 0) against a workspace that already has a live session (foreground lock holder or running daemon container). --all provisions every sandbox sandy already KNOWS about that is missing the per-sandbox state a launch creates -- pip/ since 2.6.0 (#382; relay-state/ was the target from 2.2.0 through 2.5.x, but a launch no longer creates it), which is what --reset-sandbox leaves behind, and what any launch that failed part-way leaves behind; it enumerates $SANDY_HOME/sandboxes, so a workspace that has never been launched has no directory and cannot be reached by it -- enrolling a new workspace stays a deliberate single --workspace call. A sandbox whose recorded workspace no longer exists cannot be provisioned: it is named, counted as unprepared, and makes the run exit non-zero rather than being skipped silently. Exit 0 iff every known sandbox ends with that state in place. Sub-options: --workspace PATH, --all, --dry-run, --yes.

cli_flags.name: --workspace
cli_flags.description: Target workspace directory (defaults to the current directory). Honored by the bare launch path (including -p/--rebuild/--build-only), --start, --attach, --stop, --exec, --login, --update-sessions, --reset-sandbox, --remove-sandbox, --provision, --approvals, and --accounts. NOT accepted by --gc, --stop-all, --prune-orphans, --doctor, or the other introspection flags (--print-schema/--print-state/--validate-config).
